Build-plan item 1.8 is genuinely confirmed for Linux/Claude Code 2.1.282/Python 3.11.15/dontAsk, with its scope limits stated in the doc rather than implied. 592 tests pass here (measured, matching the claim); lwb_check_proof (23 records, and --pr 57 --base 6afc545 --head efdc0af confirms the record self-declares PR 57), lwb_handoff.py --check, lwb_check_state_claims --repo ., lwb_check_prefix, lwb_check_no_instruction_dep, lwb_build.py --check (both vendor trees), lwb_check_hook_launch, lwb_validate_claude_plugin and lwb_check_commit_identity all pass at this head. The ordering trap is clean: the generator ran at da1d39a and the later commit efdc0af only MODIFIES an existing proof record, so the count stays 23 and state-claims passes.

WHY DISAGREE ANYWAY: THIS BRANCH CANNOT PASS CI, AND CANNOT BE REPAIRED IN PLACE. Commit 100f6545c541 added a literal POSIX home-directory checkout path (this container's) on three lines of an early draft of the new doc. Commit 195b942fcb86 fixed the file's final content, so the working-tree scan is clean -- CI's plain `lwb-env-leak` step is SUCCESS on this head with the REAL LWB_PRIVATE_NEEDLES secret, which I confirmed through the Actions per-job steps API, so the tree is clean against the real private-name list too, not merely against my placeholder. But scripts/lwb_check_env_leak.py --range scans the ADDED LINES OF EVERY COMMIT in the range, by explicit design (its own docstring: a leak one commit adds and a later commit in the same range removes is still caught), so no later commit on this branch can ever clear it. MEASURED, not inferred: lwb_check_env_leak.py --range 6afc545..efdc0af fails with three findings, all attributed to commit 100f6545c541 by sha, pattern class 'POSIX home directory path'. (I am deliberately not quoting the offending lines in this record -- doing so would reintroduce the leak into a tracked file and fail the same check on my own commit.) CI agrees exactly: on run 36055115298, all six `test` jobs (ubuntu/macos/windows x 3.10/3.12) fail on precisely two steps, `lwb-env-leak-history` and `lwb-lanes`, and nothing else. Repair requires rewriting 100f6545 out of the branch's history; force-push is denied in this environment. So the failure is PERMANENT for this branch.

I ALSO PROBED THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN TRUSTING THE EXPLANATION. On the #58 branch I committed a POSIX home path into the same doc, then removed it again in a second commit. Result: the working tree came back clean while --range STILL failed, naming the introducing commit by sha. The 'a later commit cannot clear it' claim is therefore verified behaviour, not a story, and the re-cut was necessary rather than cosmetic.

WHAT I RECOMMEND. Do not merge #57. Merge #58 instead: its content is identical (the only differences I found across the whole branch are one em-dash rendered as '--' in HANDOFF.md, the generated block's timestamp, and the proof record's own bookkeeping -- pr 57->58, commit sha, two re-run digests, an added env-leak command, and an 'unproven' entry explaining the re-cut), its history never contained the leak, and its CI is green on every step including `lwb-env-leak-history` with the real secret -- red only on `lwb-lanes`, which I cleared this run with reviews/58/cloud-reviewer-b.json (AGREE).
